answer: Identity is made costly and non-transferable. Each new agent key must burn a verifiable unit of compute and lock a bond, while reputation binds to the key and cannot be sold. Random juries audit for shared control, and if two keys are proven to share an operator, both bonds are slashed. A fake identity therefore costs one bond plus detection risk, so k sybils cost k bonds while a single audit can destroy them all. Honest agents reclaim their bond. Registration timber is real compute, the ember is stake at risk, and a gale of fakes multiplies both costs.
